title: Pain relief for thoracotomy. Comparison of morphine requirements using an extrapleural infusion of bupivacaine.
abstract: BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: The effectiveness of a continuous infusion of extrapleural bupivacaine for relief of postoperative pain was assessed in patients undergoing posterolateral thoracotomy under general anesthesia by comparing morphine requirements. METHODS: Bupivacaine 0.25% was infused at a rate of 5 mL/h through an unkinkable extrapleural catheter that was sited under direct vision at operation. RESULTS: Mean (+/- SD) 24-hour requirements for morphine from a patient-controlled analgesia device were 39 +/- 15 mg for the treated group and 69 +/- 26 mg in the control group (P < .006). Patients in the treated group recorded significantly smaller visual analog scores for pain both at rest (P < .005) and on movement (P < .03) compared to the control group. There were no adverse effects associated with the use of extrapleural bupivacaine in this study. CONCLUSIONS: Continuous extrapleural infusion of bupivacaine through unkinkable catheters sited during thoracotomy resulted in decreased intravenous patient-controlled analgesia use and decreased verbal categoric pain scores at rest and during movement.
